primary_diagnosis_treated: Non-Alcoholic Fatty Liver Disease / Non-Alcoholic Steatohepatitis (NAFLD/NASH)
nice_guideline_used: CG181 / NG28 (Metabolic syndrome), NG203 (Chronic kidney disease), NG136 (Hypertension)

medications.duration: Lifelong – review lipid panel at 12 weeks then annually
medications.purpose: Reduce LDL cholesterol and overall cardiovascular risk associated with NAFLD/NASH and metabolic syndrome
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG181/NG28 recommends high‑intensity statin for LDL > 190 mg/dL or high CV risk

medications.dose: 2.5 mg orally once daily, titrate every 2‑4 weeks to 5‑10 mg once daily to target BP <140/90 mmHg (or <130/80 mmHg if albuminuria)
medications.duration: Lifelong – monitor renal function and potassium at 2 weeks then every 3 months
medications.purpose: Blood pressure control, renal protection, and cardiovascular risk reduction in CKD and metabolic syndrome
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG203 advises ACE‑I as first‑line for CKD with hypertension or proteinuria

medications.duration: Lifelong – review eGFR and potassium at 2 weeks then every 6 months
medications.purpose: Renal‑protective and cardiovascular benefit in CKD, also improves NAFLD histology
medications.nice_justification: NICE TA775 (NG203) recommends SGLT2‑i for CKD with eGFR ≥20 mL/min/1.73 m², even without diabetes

medications.dose: 500 mg orally once daily with evening meal, increase by 500 mg weekly to 1000 mg twice daily as tolerated (max 2 g/day)
medications.duration: Lifelong – HbA1c review at 3 months then every 6 months; renal function review if eGFR <45
medications.purpose: Improve insulin sensitivity, aid weight loss, and lower progression from prediabetes to type 2 diabetes
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG28/CG181 recommends metformin for prediabetes/high‑risk patients when eGFR ≥30 mL/min/1.73 m²

medications.dose: 0.25 mg subcutaneously weekly, titrate every 4 weeks to 1 mg weekly as tolerated
medications.duration: Lifelong – weight, HbA1c and liver enzymes review at 3 months then annually
medications.purpose: Weight reduction, glycaemic improvement, and potential histological benefit in NASH
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG181 suggests GLP‑1 RA for obesity (BMI ≥ 30 kg/m²) with metabolic comorbidities

contraindications.reason: Accelerates CKD progression and increases cardiovascular risk (NG203)
contraindications.alternative: Use paracetamol for pain; avoid NSAIDs where possible

contraindications.reason: Increases risk of hyperkalaemia and acute kidney injury (NG203)
contraindications.alternative: Continue ACE‑I alone; add other antihypertensives if needed
Dose‑adjust or discontinue if eGFR falls below 30; monitor eGFR

contraindications.drug: SGLT2 inhibitor if eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m²
contraindications.alternative: Do not initiate below eGFR 30; reassess renal function before starting

treatment_summary: The patient has NAFLD/NASH with metabolic syndrome, pre‑diabetes, dyslipidaemia, and probable stage 3 CKD. A NICE‑aligned regimen includes high‑intensity atorvastatin, ramipril titrated to BP target, dapagliflozin for renal and cardiovascular protection, metformin for glucose control, and semaglutide for weight loss and potential NASH improvement. All drugs are compatible with his inhaled asthma therapy. Monitoring of lipids, renal function, electrolytes, HbA1c, weight and liver enzymes is outlined, and key contraindications and data gaps are flagged for further assessment.
